recommendations.title: Injury Patterns in an Elite Men's Futsal Club: A Nine-Season Cohort Study.
recommendations.authors: Carles Miñarro; Bernat de Pablo Marquez; Lore Zumeta-Olaskoaga; Dai Sugimoto; Gil Rodas; Marti Casals
recommendations.reason: The study reports injury counts and cumulative injury proportions using 671 player-seasons, but it does not report training or match exposure hours, athlete-exposures, match-exposures, a study-specific time rate, or exact derivation inputs. The paper explicitly states that precise exposure time was unavailable and that exposure data are needed to define injury incidence and burden accurately.
recommendations.studyDesign: Retrospective nine-season cohort from one elite futsal club
recommendations.dataCollectionTiming: Injuries were extracted retrospectively from club electronic medical records covering the 2014/2015 to 2022/2023 seasons.
recommendations.populationEligibility: 214 male elite futsal players across youth and senior categories
recommendations.competitionContext: Single elite club across six competitive categories and nine seasons
recommendations.dataSource: Club electronic medical records systematically maintained by club medical staff
recommendations.outcomeEligibility: 1,043 time-loss injuries with descriptive injury patterns and cumulative injury proportions
recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: Time-loss injury definitions based on IOC and UEFA consensus guidance
recommendations.reportedDenominator: 671 player-seasons used for cumulative injury proportions; no training or match exposure time
recommendations.denominatorEvidenceQuote: Although precise exposure time was not available, senior athletes participated in a higher number of training sessions and total games.
evidenceQuotes: Although precise exposure time was not available, senior athletes participated in a higher number of training sessions and total games.
